tools.name: amber-build
tools.label: Amber · system build
tools.description: tleap topology and coordinates from a PDB: RNA force field, water box and ions, ParmEd NBfix19 / 0BPh / HMR / 12-6-4, optional two-pass build with L-RNA renaming.

inputs.name: structure
inputs.label: Starting structure (PDB)
inputs.tooltip: RNA model to parameterise, e.g. the best FARFAR2 cluster centre.

sections.title: Input structure
sections.tooltip: How the starting PDB is cleaned before tleap reads it.

options.label: Prepare the PDB for tleap
options.tooltip: Write a cleaned copy of the input first: hydrogens removed (tleap rebuilds them), TER records between chains, first MODEL only. Rosetta / FARFAR2 models need this.

options.label: Remove 5′-terminal phosphates
options.tooltip: Drop P/OP1/OP2 of each chain's first residue: Amber's 5′-terminal residues (G5, A5 ...) have no phosphate.

options.label: Break chains at numbering gaps
options.tooltip: Insert a TER record where residue numbers jump, so tleap does not bond across a gap.

options.label: Remove waters from the input
options.tooltip: Crystal waters are dropped; the solvent box is built by tleap.

sections.title: Force field
sections.tooltip: RNA force field and extra parameters / libraries / leap commands.

options.label: RNA force field
options.tooltip: leaprc file for RNA. 'OL3 + CP' adds the phosphate oxygen vdW correction of Steinbrecher et al. (JCTC 2012) from the frcmod below; NBfix19 / 0BPh assume it.
choices: OL3 + CP (bsc0 χOL3, Steinbrecher phosphate vdW)

options.label: CP parameters
options.tooltip: Retyped library: the build script writes RNA_CP.lib (AmberTools' RNA.lib with the phosphate oxygens retyped OP / OR) and frcmod.cp (the CP Lennard-Jones values plus the parm10.dat bonded terms for the new types), so only phosphate oxygens change and the NBfix19 / 0BPh masks address them as @%OP / @%OR. Own frcmod: load a CP parameter file you provide (masks stay @%O2 / @%OS).

options.label: CP frcmod file
options.tooltip: Parameter file with the CP phosphate correction: a name in leap's search path / the step folder, or an absolute path.

options.label: Extra parameter files
options.tooltip: One frcmod file per line, loaded with loadamberparams after the force field (e.g. frcmod.LRNA).

options.label: Extra residue libraries
options.tooltip: One library (.lib / .off) per line, loaded with loadOff (e.g. LRNA.lib).

options.label: Leap commands before parameter files
options.tooltip: Inserted right after the leaprc files, e.g. addAtomTypes for new atom types.

options.label: Leap commands before loadpdb
options.tooltip: Inserted before the PDB is read, e.g. addPdbResMap entries.

options.label: Leap commands after loadpdb
options.tooltip: Inserted after the PDB is read and before solvation, e.g. bond commands.

sections.title: Solvent & ions
sections.tooltip: Water box and ions (tleap solvateoct / solvatebox and addIonsRand).

options.label: Water model
options.tooltip: Water model; its leaprc also loads the matching monovalent / divalent ion parameters.

options.label: Box shape
options.tooltip: Truncated octahedron (solvateoct) needs ~30 % less water than a rectangular box.

options.label: Buffer
options.tooltip: Minimum distance between the RNA and the box edge.

options.label: Neutralise with monovalent cations
options.tooltip: addIonsRand <cation> 0 neutralises the RNA's phosphate charge.

options.label: Cation
options.tooltip: Monovalent cation for neutralisation and salt.

options.label: Mg²⁺ ions
options.tooltip: Number of Mg²⁺ ions (residue MG) added at random positions.

options.label: Balance Mg²⁺ with Cl⁻
options.tooltip: Add two Cl⁻ per Mg²⁺ so the box stays neutral.

options.label: Extra salt pairs
options.tooltip: Additional cation/Cl⁻ pairs (≈ concentration [M] × number of waters / 55.5).

options.label: Mg²⁺ Lennard-Jones model
options.tooltip: 12-6: the Li & Merz parameters loaded with the water model. 12-6-4 (Li & Merz): loads frcmod.ions234lm_1264_<water> and adds the C4 terms with ParmEd add12_6_4 (Amber only; GROMACS cannot represent C4). microMg / nanoMg (Grotz, Cruz-León & Schwierz): optimised 12-6 Mg²⁺ with explicit Mg²⁺-RNA pair terms tuned to phosphate binding - written as a frcmod plus ParmEd changeLJPair lines, and carried into GROMACS as [ nonbond_params ]. microMg keeps the experimental (µs) water exchange; nanoMg exchanges water faster for better sampling of ion binding.

options.label: Mg²⁺-Cl⁻ pair term
options.tooltip: Apply the authors' Mg²⁺-Cl⁻ pair term (optimised with their Cl⁻ model; Amber's Cl⁻ parameters are kept for everything else). Without it Mg²⁺-Cl⁻ follows the combination rule with the optimised Mg²⁺, which is not a published combination and gives much too strong Mg²⁺-Cl⁻ contacts.

sections.title: ParmEd
sections.tooltip: Topology edits applied with ParmEd after tleap (leap cannot reload a prmtop).

options.label: NBfix19 (gHBfix19 as LJ pairs)
options.tooltip: Off-diagonal Lennard-Jones terms for -NH...N- and -OH...O(phosphate) pairs (Kuehrova & Mlynsky JCTC 2019; Mlynsky et al. 2026). The masks assume OL3 + CP.

options.label: 0BPh pairs
options.tooltip: Extra H5/H4 – O5' Lennard-Jones pairs of the 0BPh modification (Mlýnský et al. 2023): masks @%OR with the CP library, @%OS otherwise.

options.label: Separate HO and O2 Lennard-Jones types first
options.tooltip: addLJType @%HO and @%O2 before the pair changes. tleap merges atom types with equal LJ parameters: HO shares its LJ type with water HW and O2 with base carbonyl O, so without this the HO-O2 / HO-OS pairs also change water-H and carbonyl-O interactions.

options.label: Hydrogen mass repartitioning
options.tooltip: ParmEd HMassRepartition (hydrogens 3.024 Da) so MD can use a 4 fs time step with SHAKE.

options.label: Extra ParmEd commands
options.tooltip: Added before outparm, e.g. the L-RNA changeLJPair lines.

sections.title: L-RNA
sections.tooltip: L-RNA residue names for leap (the library and parameters go under Force field).

options.label: Name L-nucleotides for leap
options.tooltip: Before tleap, residues whose sugar chirality (C1'/C3'/C4') is L get L-RNA names (Dudek & Trylska: LA LC LG LU, terminals LA5/LA3 ...), the other RNA residues Amber names. Runs the PDB tools that MDATK copies into the step folder (replaces to_lrna.sh); a structure without L residues is only checked.

options.label: Force L for
options.tooltip: Residues that are L whatever their geometry says (overrides the detection), e.g. 'C:45-73', 'A:45-73, A:80-90' or 'C' for a whole chain.

options.label: 5'/3' terminal names
options.tooltip: LA5/LA3 ... at chain ends as in nucleic12_LRNA.lib. Off: plain LA/LC/LG/LU at the ends (as to_lrna.sh wrote), for libraries that map terminals with addPdbResMap.

options.label: NBfix19 / 0BPh / CP for L-RNA
options.tooltip: Declare the L-RNA library's atom types for tleap (addAtomTypes) and add the NBfix19 / 0BPh pairs for its bridging-oxygen type (HO, H5, H4 against LD, as for OS / OR in D-RNA). ParmEd skips them when the structure has no L residues. The CP correction of L residues comes with the L-RNA parameter file (e.g. frcmod.LRNA).

options.label: L-RNA atom types
options.tooltip: Atom types of the L-RNA library declared as sp3 oxygens before it is loaded; the first one is the bridging phosphate oxygen used in the NBfix19 / 0BPh pairs.

options.label: Two-pass build
options.tooltip: L-RNA naming -> dry tleap -> ParmEd -> ambpdb -> solvated tleap -> ParmEd. The ambpdb PDB keeps the dry topology's residue names (Amber terminal names are re-applied).

options.label: Also save a PDB of the built system
options.tooltip: tleap savepdb after solvation - handy for a visual check.

sections.title: Environment
sections.tooltip: How the generated scripts find the programs.

options.label: Conda environment
options.tooltip: Activate this conda environment at the top of the script (eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"; conda activate <name>). Leave empty when the programs are already on PATH.

tools.name: amber-restraints
tools.label: Amber · helix restraints
tools.description: Helix-preserving DISANG distance restraints for the hydrogen bonds of every base pair in the secondary structure (looked up in the final topology).

inputs.name: topology
inputs.label: Topology (parm7)
inputs.tooltip: The solvated (and ParmEd-modified) topology the MD runs with.

inputs.name: secstruct
inputs.label: Secondary structure
inputs.tooltip: Optional: a dot-bracket file or a FARFAR2 step; otherwise type it below.

sections.title: Base pairs
sections.tooltip: Each G–C pair gets three, each A–U pair two distance restraints (flat-bottom window r1–r4).

options.label: Sequence
options.tooltip: RNA sequence in topology order; chains separated by spaces, '&' or new lines (optionally 'A: GGCAC...'). Not needed when a secondary-structure file is connected.

options.label: Secondary structure
options.tooltip: Dot-bracket notation for the whole sequence; '()', '[]', '{}' and '<>' pairs are restrained. Strand separators (spaces, '&') are ignored.

options.label: Residue offset
options.tooltip: Topology residue number = position in the sequence + offset (use when the topology has extra residues before the RNA).

options.label: Restrain G·U wobble pairs
options.tooltip: Also restrain G·U pairs (G O6–U N3, G N1–U O2). Off: only Watson–Crick G–C and A–U pairs are restrained.

options.label: r1
options.tooltip: Lower distance where the linear restraint wall starts (Å).

options.label: r2
options.tooltip: Start of the flat bottom (Å).

options.label: r3
options.tooltip: End of the flat bottom (Å).

options.label: r4
options.tooltip: Upper distance where the restraint turns linear (Å).

options.label: rk2
options.tooltip: Force constant below r2 (kcal/mol/Å²).

options.label: rk3
options.tooltip: Force constant above r3 (kcal/mol/Å²).

tools.name: amber-md
tools.label: Amber · MD stages
tools.description: pmemd input files (minimisation, heating, equilibration, production) and the scripts that run them with pmemd, pmemd.cuda or pmemd.MPI.

inputs.name: restraints
inputs.label: Restraints (DISANG)
inputs.tooltip: Needed by stages with 'Helix distance restraints'.

sections.title: Engine
sections.tooltip: Which pmemd binary runs the stages and how.

options.label: Amber version
options.tooltip: Version the files target (local Amber 26 or cluster Amber 24); the input format is the same, the version is recorded in the scripts.

options.label: MD engine
options.tooltip: Program for the MD stages.

options.label: MPI processes
options.tooltip: Processes for pmemd.MPI.

options.label: MPI launcher
options.tooltip: Command placed before pmemd.MPI; {n} is replaced by the process count (srun on SLURM clusters).

options.label: GPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES)
options.tooltip: Optional GPU index for pmemd.cuda.

options.label: Minimisation engine
options.tooltip: pmemd.cuda can stop on bad initial contacts; the CPU pmemd is more forgiving.

options.label: Input coordinates have velocities
options.tooltip: Tick when the starting rst7 is a restart of an earlier MD run, so the first MD stage can continue it (irest=1).

options.label: Positional restraint reference
options.tooltip: Coordinates used as -ref for positional restraints.

options.label: Separate production script
options.tooltip: Production stages go into their own script (e.g. to run them on a cluster).

options.label: Skip finished stages
options.tooltip: When the script is re-run, stages whose output file already has pmemd's final timing lines are skipped (resumes an interrupted run).

sections.title: Stages
sections.tooltip: Stages run in order; each starts from the previous stage's restart file.

options.label: Name
options.tooltip: Short stage name used in file names (letters, digits, hyphens), e.g. min1, heat, eq, prod.

options.label: Title
options.tooltip: First line of the mdin file (a free comment).

options.label: Type
options.tooltip: Energy minimisation (imin=1) or molecular dynamics (imin=0).

options.label: Cycles (maxcyc)
options.tooltip: Total minimisation cycles.

options.label: Steepest-descent cycles (ncyc)
options.tooltip: With ntmin=1: cycles of steepest descent before switching to conjugate gradient.

options.label: Method (ntmin)
options.tooltip: Minimisation algorithm.

options.label: Steps (nstlim)
options.tooltip: Number of MD steps.

options.label: Time step (dt)
options.tooltip: Time step in ps (0.002 with SHAKE; 0.004 needs hydrogen mass repartitioning).

options.label: Velocities
options.tooltip: auto: new velocities (irest=0, ntx=1) after a minimisation or at the start, otherwise continue the previous stage (irest=1, ntx=5).

options.label: Ensemble
options.tooltip: Constant volume (ntb=1) or constant pressure (ntb=2, ntp>0).

options.label: Thermostat
options.tooltip: Temperature control (ntt).

options.label: Collision frequency (gamma_ln)
options.tooltip: Langevin collision frequency in ps⁻¹.

options.label: Coupling time (tautp)
options.tooltip: Berendsen thermostat time constant (ps).

options.label: Randomisation interval (vrand)
options.tooltip: Andersen: steps between velocity randomisations.

options.label: Initial temperature (tempi)
options.tooltip: Temperature of the new velocities (K).

options.label: Temperature (temp0)
options.tooltip: Reference temperature (K).

options.label: Ramp the temperature
options.tooltip: Raise temp0 linearly from tempi with an nmropt TEMP0 schedule instead of jumping to temp0 at once.

options.label: Ramp length (steps)
options.tooltip: Steps over which the temperature rises; the rest of the stage runs at temp0.

options.label: Barostat
options.tooltip: Pressure control in NPT.

options.label: Pressure (pres0)
options.tooltip: Reference pressure (bar).

options.label: Relaxation time (taup)
options.tooltip: Berendsen barostat time constant (ps).

options.label: MC volume moves every (mcbarint)
options.tooltip: Steps between Monte Carlo volume moves.

options.label: Pressure scaling (ntp)
options.tooltip: Isotropic (ntp=1) or anisotropic (ntp=2).

options.label: SHAKE bonds to hydrogen
options.tooltip: ntc=2, ntf=2 (needed for dt > 0.001 ps).

options.label: SHAKE tolerance (tol)
options.tooltip: Relative SHAKE tolerance; empty uses Amber's default (1.0e-5).

options.label: Random seed (ig)
options.tooltip: Empty: a new seed each run (ig=-1).

options.label: Cutoff (cut)
options.tooltip: Direct-space non-bonded cutoff (Å).

options.label: Positional restraints
options.tooltip: Harmonic restraints to the reference coordinates (ntr=1, restraint_wt, restraintmask).

options.label: Restraint mask
options.tooltip: Amber mask of restrained atoms; empty restrains the solute (':1-N' when the residue count is known, otherwise everything except water and ions).

options.label: Restraint weight
options.tooltip: restraint_wt in kcal/mol/Å².

options.label: Helix distance restraints
options.tooltip: nmropt=1 with DISANG=<restraint file> (the step's restraint input).

options.label: Print restraint violations (LISTOUT=POUT)
options.tooltip: Writes the restraint violation summary to the output file.

options.label: Energy output every (ntpr)
options.tooltip: Steps between energy printouts.

options.label: Trajectory frame every (ntwx)
options.tooltip: Steps between trajectory frames (0: no trajectory).

options.label: Restart file every (ntwr)
options.tooltip: Steps between restart-file updates.

options.label: NetCDF trajectory (ioutfm=1)
options.tooltip: Binary NetCDF instead of ASCII.

options.label: Wrap into the box (iwrap=1)
options.tooltip: Wrap molecules into the primary box in the output.

options.label: Split into segments
options.tooltip: Run this stage as N consecutive pmemd runs (e.g. to fit cluster wall-time limits); file names get -001, -002 ...

options.label: Production stage
options.tooltip: Its trajectory is passed on to analysis / visualisation steps and goes into the separate production script.

options.label: Extra &cntrl settings
options.tooltip: Additional name=value settings added inside &cntrl (they override generated values with the same name).

options.label: Extra namelists
options.tooltip: Text added after &cntrl, e.g. an &ewald namelist.

options.label: Dry PDB before production
options.tooltip: cpptraj strips water and ions from the last restart of the main script (before the production script) - for a visual check of the equilibrated structure.

options.label: Strip mask
options.tooltip: cpptraj mask of atoms removed in the dry PDB / trajectory.

options.label: Dry, imaged production trajectory
options.tooltip: cpptraj autoimage + strip of the production trajectories (and the matching dry topology) for visualisation.

options.label: Strip mask (trajectory)
options.tooltip: cpptraj mask removed from the dry trajectory.

tools.name: structure-builder
tools.label: Structure builder (MDATK)
tools.description: Starting structures without external programs: ideal A-form RNA helices (D or L), base mutations keeping the glycosidic frame (with compensatory partners), and rigid-body fitting into a density map.

inputs.name: pdb
inputs.label: Model (PDB)
inputs.tooltip: The structure to mutate or to fit.

inputs.name: map
inputs.label: Density map
inputs.tooltip: MRC / CCP4 map for the rigid-body fit.

outputs.name: secstruct
outputs.label: Secondary structure
outputs.tooltip: Duplex pairs of the ideal helix (Watson-Crick and G·U, antiparallel only), e.g. for helix restraints.

options.label: Build
options.tooltip: Ideal helix: a new A-form duplex or single strand. Mutate: swap bases of the connected PDB. Fit: place the connected PDB in the map.

options.label: Sequence (5'->3')
options.tooltip: Strand 1; T is read as U.

options.label: Partner strand
options.tooltip: Complement (the canonical partners of the pairing: Watson-Crick for wc), none (single strand) or a sequence typed below.

options.label: Partner (5'->3')
options.tooltip: Same length as strand 1; mismatches and G·U wobbles are allowed (reported).

options.label: Pairing
options.tooltip: Base-pair geometry of the duplex: Watson-Crick (antiparallel A-form, default), reverse Watson-Crick / Hoogsteen / Hoogsteen-Hoogsteen (parallel strands) or reverse Hoogsteen (antiparallel). For the Hoogsteen pairings strand 1 is the purine strand.

options.label: Triplex
options.tooltip: A third strand in the major groove on the Hoogsteen edge of the strand-1 purines (Watson-Crick duplex only).
choices: purine motif: reverse Hoogsteen, antiparallel (A·A-U, G·G-C)

options.label: Third strand
options.tooltip: The canonical motif bases (U / C+ or A / G on A / G) or a sequence typed below.

options.label: Third strand (5'->3')
options.tooltip: Same length as strand 1; mismatches are allowed (reported).

options.label: Chirality
options.tooltip: D: right-handed. L: the mirror image (left-handed, L-nucleotides).

options.label: Chain ids
options.tooltip: Strand 1, strand 2 (and 3 of a triplex; default C).

options.label: Residue names
options.tooltip: Name scheme of mdatk.pdbtools.

options.label: 5'/3' terminal names
options.tooltip: For the schemes with terminal variants (Amber, CCD).

options.label: 5'-phosphate
options.tooltip: Keep P/OP1/OP2/OP3 on the 5' ends (the Amber 5' units have none).

options.label: Hydrogens
options.tooltip: Add all hydrogens (default: heavy atoms only).

options.label: Mutations
options.tooltip: Chain:residue + new base, comma separated.

options.label: Compensatory partner mutations
options.tooltip: Change the Watson-Crick / G·U partner of every mutated base to the complement unless it is mutated explicitly.

options.label: Keep G·U pairs
options.tooltip: A G or U facing U / G keeps its partner (wobble) instead of the Watson-Crick complement.

options.label: Map resolution
options.tooltip: Width of the simulated model map.

options.label: Search
options.tooltip: Global: all orientations and positions. Local: refine the model as placed.

options.label: Angular step
options.tooltip: Rotation sampling of the global search.

tools.name: restraint-dicts
tools.label: Restraint dictionaries · acedrg / eLBOW
tools.description: mmCIF restraint dictionaries for residues Coot / Phenix do not know - the L-RNA terminal variants 0A5/0A3 ... - generated by acedrg or phenix.elbow from SMILES and renamed to the model's CCD atom names.

inputs.name: structure
inputs.label: Model (PDB)
inputs.tooltip: Optional: generate the 5'/3' variants this model needs (its L-RNA chain ends); without a model all eight variants are written.

sections.title: Program
sections.tooltip: Which program generates the restraints.

options.label: Program
options.tooltip: acedrg (CCP4) or phenix.elbow (Phenix) builds the restraints from the SMILES; MDATK then renames the atoms to the CCD names the model uses.

options.label: Phenix version
options.tooltip: Installed Phenix release.

options.label: Phenix installation
options.tooltip: Top folder of the Phenix installation; the script sources its phenix_env.sh. Leave empty when phenix.elbow is already on PATH.

options.label: CCP4 setup script
options.tooltip: Sourced before acedrg runs (ccp4.setup-sh of the CCP4 installation). Leave empty when acedrg is already on PATH.

options.label: Extra arguments
options.tooltip: Added to every acedrg / phenix.elbow command line.

sections.title: Residues
sections.tooltip: Which residue codes get a dictionary.

options.label: Residues
options.tooltip: Model: the 5'/3' variants the connected model needs (all eight when no model is connected or it does not exist yet). The four parents 0A/0C/0G/0U are CCD entries that Coot and Phenix already know.

options.label: Codes
options.tooltip: Residue codes separated by spaces or commas; codes that are not in the table need a custom SMILES.

options.label: Polymer group
options.tooltip: _chem_comp.group of the dictionaries. RNA lets Coot / Phenix link the residue to its neighbours like the CCD's L-nucleotides; non-polymer makes it a free ligand.

options.label: Custom SMILES
options.tooltip: One 'code = SMILES' per line. For a code of the table the SMILES replaces the built-in one and must describe the same molecule and stereochemistry; other codes keep the atom names the program invents.

sections.title: PubChem
sections.tooltip: Optional SMILES lookup (network).

options.label: Fetch SMILES from PubChem when writing (network)
options.tooltip: Off: no network access. On: the isomeric SMILES of the compounds below is downloaded from PubChem (PUG REST) when the step's files are written, checked against the code's atom graph and stereochemistry, and used instead of the built-in SMILES.

options.label: PubChem compounds
options.tooltip: One 'code = CID' (or compound name) per line.

options.label: Timeout
options.tooltip: Seconds to wait for PubChem.

tools.name: farfar2
tools.label: Rosetta · FARFAR2 (rna_denovo)
tools.description: De novo RNA 3D models with Rosetta FARFAR2: FASTA / secstruct from a sequence and dot-bracket, optional fixed helices and cryo-EM density, parallel seeds.

inputs.name: structure
inputs.label: Fixed helices (-s)
inputs.tooltip: PDB of pre-built helices kept rigid during assembly (-s).

inputs.name: map
inputs.label: Density map
inputs.tooltip: Cryo-EM map (MRC/CCP4) to fit the models into.

sections.title: Sequence & structure
sections.tooltip: What to fold.

options.label: Write FASTA and secstruct from the fields below
options.tooltip: Generate the Rosetta FASTA (one entry per chain, lower case, A:1-16 numbering) and the secstruct file. Off: use existing files.

options.label: Sequence
options.tooltip: One chain per line or chains separated by spaces / '&' (optionally 'A: ggcac...'). Residues are numbered continuously across chains.

options.label: Secondary structure
options.tooltip: Dot-bracket for the whole sequence (strand separators optional). Paired bases must be complementary (G–C, A–U, G–U) or rna_denovo stops.

options.label: FASTA name
options.tooltip: Name on the FASTA header lines; empty uses the project name.

options.label: Existing FASTA
options.tooltip: FASTA file to use instead.

options.label: Existing secstruct
options.tooltip: Secondary structure file to use instead (dot-bracket on line 1).

sections.title: Sampling
sections.tooltip: rna_denovo options.

options.label: Models per run (-nstruct)
options.tooltip: Models written by each run.

options.label: Monte Carlo cycles (-cycles)
options.tooltip: Fragment-assembly cycles per model (Rosetta default 10 000).

options.label: Full-atom refinement (-minimize_rna)
options.tooltip: High-resolution minimisation after assembly - strongly recommended.

options.label: Fixed stems (-fixed_stems)
options.tooltip: Seed every helix of the secondary structure with Watson–Crick pairs.

options.label: Base-pair-step moves
options.tooltip: -rna:denovo:bps_moves (helix flexibility by base pair step fragments).

options.label: Heat (-heat)
options.tooltip: Randomise torsions before assembly.

options.label: Close loops (-close_loops)
options.tooltip: Close chain breaks by cyclic coordinate descent after fragment moves.

options.label: Fuzz fragments
options.tooltip: -fuzz_fragments value (0: not set).

options.label: Autofilter (-autofilter)
options.tooltip: Keep only models that score among the best during the run.

options.label: Filter low-res base pairs
options.tooltip: -filter_lores_base_pairs: discard models missing the secondary-structure pairs.

options.label: Filter chain closure
options.tooltip: -filter_chain_closure: discard models with open chain breaks.

options.label: … also halfway
options.tooltip: -filter_chain_closure_halfway

options.label: … distance
options.tooltip: -filter_chain_closure_distance (Å).

options.label: Coordinate constraints in minimiser
options.tooltip: -rna:denovo:minimize:minimizer_use_coordinate_constraints
